title: What Is Monitored Containment? The Council of AI Boundary Posture
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle -- answer-first seed for the Council of AI containment glossary; the verified measurement credential ties boundary telemetry to an auditable record
body: Monitored containment is the Council of AI's boundary posture: a system's behavior is continuously instrumented and watched, rather than claimed to be impossible to cross. The honest alternative to 'provable isolation' -- which no one can actually guarantee for a general-purpose system -- is to instrument every boundary and prove that each crossing is observed, logged, and attributable. Monitored containment does not assert a model can never misbehave; it asserts that if it does, the event is captured in a signed record and tied to a verified measurement credential, so an auditor can reconstruct who ran what, when, and against which controls. Concretely, the posture has three commitments. (1) Boundary instrumentation: every inference, tool call, and output is time-stamped and logged with model identity and control status. (2) Signed provenance: each measurement is wrapped in a verified measurement credential -- a signature over the canonical body that lets any third party confirm the reading was issued by the measurement operator and not altered afterward. (3) Incident traceability: any boundary event lands in the Council of AI Containment Incident Index, so a mislabeled, unmarked, or out-of-policy output is traceable to a specific event rather than an anonymous failure. The practical difference is auditability: provable isolation offers a binary guarantee no one can deliver, while monitored containment offers a checkable, signed chain of evidence anyone can verify. For a regulator, a buyer, or an auditor, that is the difference between trusting a claim and verifying a measurement.
